title: Curriculum-Easy LR Sweep
subtitle: Three learning-rate arms RL-training the same 30B MoE instruct model on real terminal-agent tasks in Daytona sandboxes, racing to step 50. How each arm is trending, what every metric means, and what actually happened to all those Slurm jobs.

explainer.title: What is this experiment?
paragraphs: Unlike the GSM8K campaign that validated the stack, this one is a **research** run: the model is graded on whether it actually completes a terminal task — it drives a shell inside a Daytona sandbox under the Terminus-2 harness, and the reward is binary (task done / not done) on the `tasktrove_curriculum_easy_rl511` task set.

All three arms are **identical except one lever**: the learning rate (1e-6 / 3e-6 / 5e-6). Same seed, same data, same 6 GH200 nodes, same 8 rollouts per task — so any daylight between the curves is caused by that one lever. The 3e-6 baseline arm started a day earlier and is correspondingly further along; compare arms **at equal step**, never at the right-hand edge.

Read the reward curve with care. Each point is 128 binary rollouts, so its noise floor is around **±0.04** even when nothing is changing — and step-to-step swings of 0.2 are routine. Twenty-five steps in, no arm shows a trend that clears that noise. The honest current answer is *no separation yet*, not *it works* or *it fails*.

timeline.title: The job war — every Slurm attempt, Aug 16 04:00 → now
timeline.how: Each bar is one Slurm job; the dot at its end is how it died. Two enemies dominate. **Ghost-GPU OOM:** a node is returned to the pool before the previous job's GPU memory is actually released, so ours lands on a card already holding 60–85 GB of someone else's residue and dies at model load, checkpoint load, or the first backward peak. **EP/FSDP2 backward hang:** a known collective deadlock in expert-parallel backward with no upstream fix — the log simply stops and the job has to be scancelled. The defense is the same either way: checkpoint every 5 steps, resume, exclude the crime scene, relaunch. Nothing but the steps since the last checkpoint was ever lost.

notes.text: Metrics come from the trainer's own WandB runs, which log **offline** on Jupiter — one run per Slurm attempt, under each experiment dir. They are rsynced off the cluster and `wandb sync`ed into lukeleeai/jupiter-currease30b-grpo, then stitched per arm latest-attempt-wins per step. Nothing here updates on its own: every refresh is a manual sync. Job IDs, nodes and windows are read from each attempt's wandb-metadata.json and from sacct; fates are cross-checked against the operator incident ledger and the driver logs.

Reward is binary task completion averaged over 128 rollouts, so it is far noisier step-to-step than a math-accuracy curve — a single step's wobble means nothing. The metric to watch is **frac_groups_mixed**: only groups where some of the 8 rollouts succeeded and some failed produce any gradient under GRPO. All-wrong and all-correct groups contribute exactly zero, and right now they are about three quarters of every batch.

The **5e-6 arm's KL is climbing about four times faster than the baseline's** — 0.0025 to 0.0117 across its first 10 steps, versus 0.0026 to 0.0045 across the baseline's 25. That is the learning rate doing what a learning rate does, and it is the first place a too-hot arm would show itself. Its entropy is also drifting down (0.168 to 0.155) while the baseline's holds flat. Worth watching; not yet worth acting on.

Truncation is **zero** on every arm — no rollout is hitting the 32k context wall — and the TIS importance ratio sits at 1.000, so the off-policy correction is not straining. The step-to-step gaps in grad-norm are async-trainer steps where a partial batch was discarded, not failures.
